body:
The next game-maths audit checks finite movement, signed rounding and retained state against the actual maintained aiming model. The selected results agree with the published lessons; no lesson or model correction is proposed.

Ten diagnostic geometry fixtures distinguish swept contact from endpoint-only sampling and finite segments from infinite lines. Nine signed rounding cases, nine directions, all 10,800 declared angle-grid/scale velocity combinations and eighteen selected two-axis position traces pass. The original five model tests pass. Two wrong geometry policies fail with nonzero exits; the initial signed-zero verifier error is retained separately.

The report links the existing six-unit objective map, verifies those sources are unchanged, and prepares three optional learner tasks with separate assessor notes. It records the stale publication-status README finding in samples #94 and the bounded correction. No fresh browser/native/learner qualification is claimed.

Evidence identities, all thirteen manifest entries, local links, missing-shot rejection, Ruff and focused prose checks pass. Commit hooks pass with one existing advisory on unchanged specification prose. #114/#115/#124 stay open; learner effectiveness and the separate VoiceOver/touch limits remain unverified.
title: Qualify aiming movement and rounding boundaries
